title: Factory follow-ups: guard gaps, npm allow-list, tests and docs
request: Fix the open factory follow-ups: shell redirects bypass the control-plane approval rule; combined git push flags like -fu bypass the force-push check; backslash-escaped quotes hide commands from the protected-path scan; npm run * is auto-allowed; a test holds a fake key that matches the secret pattern; a weak CLI test; two PIPELINE.md notes (F new branch step, --trivial skips review)

criteria.text: No factory source file matches the guard's own secret pattern: the fake key in guard.spec.mjs is built from pieces, and a new test proves it for every file under factory/spec, factory/hooks and factory/bin

The guard fails closed: any internal error (bad config JSON, bad custom regex, null blockedCommands) blocks Bash commands with exit 2; Edit and Write fall back to safe default rules and ask, so the config stays repairable (spawn tests with a malformed config)
A backslash plus newline cannot hide a command: the push-to-main, force-push and protected-path-delete examples listed in the plan are blocked
Backslash-escaped quotes no longer hide commands (the two example forms in the plan, double-quote and dollar-single-quote, are blocked); no existing test changed; the quote replacer cannot crash

git push with combined short flags that contain f (for example -fu and -uf) and plus-prefixed refspecs are blocked; -u, --force-with-lease and a push followed by an unrelated delete-with-f command stay allowed

Bash writes to control-plane files ask the human (redirects, tee, cp, mv, install, ln, sed -i, dd of=, truncate, rm, curl -o, git checkout or restore from a ref, git apply, patch, python or node -c/-e with a literal path); reads stay silent; a block always wins over an ask; MultiEdit is in the hook matcher

The npm, node and playwright allow rules are tightened to explicit script names; deploy, publish and release scripts are denied; the installer generates allow rules only for scripts the target has and never adds a blanket npm run rule; nothing becomes more permissive
The check command with a double-dash override is refused unless the check name is configured; the factory specs run as a non-required check; .github/CODEOWNERS covers the control-plane paths

cli.spec asserts READY and NOT READY explicitly (proved by mutation: dropping the review makes the old test pass and the new one fail); the PIPELINE.md Stage 1 branch order and the --trivial rule are fixed in PIPELINE.md, the skills and the README, with a docs spec

README Known limits states honestly what shell-write matching covers and what it does not; all factory specs pass; the repo checks pass (integrity, typecheck, lint, knip, build, unit); no existing assertion weakened

notes.text: Plan: scratchpad/PLAN-factory-follow-ups.md (architect and security-reliability merged by the Director). Edits to factory/**, .claude/settings.json and .factory/config.json ask the human (Doug asked for these follow-ups; tightening only). Exact attack strings live in the planned tests, not in these criteria, because the guard blocks quoted prose that contains them.
